why: Operator, 2026-10-03, on the Medium review: a drama series' episode longer than an hour -- filling a 90-minute or 2-hour slot with commercials -- is often released on its own as a TV movie, even when the series is not flagged Anthology and the episode is not Standalone, Special or Pilot. Such an Episode with a USER-SUPPLIED title is a candidate for a Basic record: scored on the Basic profile and capped into Review, never auto-matched. Shaped on Medium row 46953 (L'Esprit de famille, 2000, 93 min against a 90-minute episode whose series carries no class), which a reviewer confirmed, and which 2.16.0's exhaustive cross-type rules had made INVISIBLE to the reviewer: the true record scored Reject and recovered Rejects are not shown. Pins both halves: eligible (at or above the Review floor) and capped (never Accept, every field agreeing). Pair with crosstype-related-altid-review-ceiling, an untyped episode of ordinary length that must stay ineligible: a gate that ignores length passes one and fails the other.
